newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ENGLAND REPRIMANDED BY MATCH REFEREE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND REPRIMANDED BY MATCH REFEREE.

text.p: England were reprimanded and warned for excessive appealing by International Cricket Council (ICC) match referee Hanumant Singh after the fourth day's play in the first test against Zimbabwe at Queen's Club on Saturday.
Singh discussed the matter with England captain Mike Atherton, coach David Lloyd and manager John Barclay and later released a statement.

"With regard to the method of appealing where a bunch of close in fielders run towards the umpire in a chorus of appeal, to my mind (this) contravenes the spirit of the game and brings the game into disrepute," he said in the statement.
"I have issued a reprimand to the team management and a repeat will warrant a suitable fine in the future."
England tour manager John Barclay said that he was not aware that Singh had intended to make the matter public but accepted the rebuke.

"We take it on board and the team has been informed," he said. "In mitigation, it was a good day for us and the enthusiasm of trying to bowl Zimbabwe out gave a lively approach to appealing. We will try to modify that enthusiasm on the last day."

In the final session England had four men clustered around the bat for the spin of Phil Tufnell and Robert Croft. The worst "chorus" came in the penultimate over of the day when England were convinced that night-watchman Bryan Strang had given a bat-pad catch to Nick Knight off Tufnell.

New Zealand umpire Steve Dunne turned the appeal down, a decision vindicated by television replays which clearly showed the ball had come off the batsman's elbow, and a posse of England fielders made no attempt to disguise their displeasure.
